name: SBI Cards and Payment Services Ltd
title: SBI Cards and Payment Services Ltd - 543066 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Credit cards: credit cost falling (7.7% gross, down 55bps QoQ) and GNPA 2.41%, but receivables growth only 2% YoY, revolver on downward bias, and cost-to-income guided 55-58%.

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 PAT rose 14% YoY to INR609 crore on lower credit cost (7.7%), though FY27 cost-to-income guided at 55-58%.
summary.overview: SBI Cards reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR5,187 crore (+7% YoY) and PAT of INR609 crore (+14% YoY), helped by gross credit cost falling 55 bps QoQ to 7.7% and GNPA down 46 bps QoQ to 2.41%. Receivables grew only about 2% YoY to INR56,926 crore, and management declined to guide on asset growth, tying it to card acquisition. FY26 PAT was INR2,167 crore (+13% YoY), with cost-to-income at 55.3% for the year after higher corporate-spend passback costs. Management expects revolver rates to drift down and is leaning on instalment lending to offset.

financial_highlights.change: management overlay retained at INR220 crore

segments.name: Card acquisition
segments.commentary: 917,000 new accounts added in Q4 against a 0.9-1.0 million quarterly target; FY26 sourcing mix 54% open market and 46% banca. Management said next quarter is expected in a similar range.

segments.name: Spends
segments.commentary: Q4 total spends above INR1.15 trillion (+31% YoY); retail spends INR89,786 crore (+13% YoY). FY26 total spends INR4.3 trillion, retail INR3.54 trillion (+15%). Online share of retail spends 62.5% in FY26; spend market share 18.1%.

segments.name: Receivables and revolve
segments.commentary: Receivables INR56,926 crore (~+2% YoY). Interest-earning assets 54%, revolver balance 22%; revolve rate has been 22-24% over two years with a slight downward bias expected in FY27.

segments.name: Other income
segments.commentary: Q4 other income elevated by one-offs: provision release and a tax-matter provision added in FY26; GST included in other income, PIDF reduction booked in expenses.

guidance_outlook: Cost-to-income expected in the 55-58% range for FY27, with no major step-up from corporate spends.
NIM expected to remain stable, at risk from any significant rise in cost of funds.
Credit cost expected to moderate further in FY27, dependent on geopolitical and macro developments.
No guidance on asset (receivables) growth; asset growth expected to follow card acquisition.
Medium-term ROA target of 4% to 4.5%, described as achievable.
No cost-of-funds guidance for FY27; around 70-75% of borrowings are floating (T-bill or repo linked) and reprice in 60-90 day buckets.
capex_capacity: No capex plans, capacity figures, utilisation data or commissioning timelines were discussed on the call; the call covered only card acquisition volumes (917,000 new accounts in Q4 vs 0.9-1.0 million quarterly target, expected to be in a similar range next quarter) and asset growth tied to acquisition, with no asset growth guidance given.
Digital onboarding via SBI Card Sprint is described as growing in share of new account acquisitions; no capacity or cost figures were disclosed for it.
Management said it is poised to harness AI and ML investments in FY27 for product development, service delivery and collections; no capex amount or timeline was given.
Collections infrastructure, digital and physical, was strengthened during the year; no capex or capacity quantification was provided.
demand_pricing: Industry credit card spends grew ~12% YoY to INR23.62 trillion in FY26 per RBI; cards-in-force above 118.6 million; SBI Card cards-in-force share 18.6%.
Management attributed muted industry card growth to issuers tightening underwriting after asset quality issues, with few new-to-credit customers being acquired.
Banca NTC/NTCC share estimated at 20-30% of banca-sourced customers; Q4 new-sourcing mix 70% salaried.
Rental spends are now a very small category after fee levy; UPI-on-credit growth 10% in Q4 vs Q3.
Management said FY26 corporate spends (with passback costs) raised both income and opex, thinning margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why is new account addition lower, and what is the cost-to-income outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 acquisition of 917,000 was on track with the 0.9-1.0 million target; cost-to-income guided 55-58% for FY27 as corporate-spend passback costs normalise, not employee cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revolver downside plan and cost-of-funds outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a revolver floor; first offset is instalment lending rather than cutting rewards. Cost of funds guidance deferred given RBI and geopolitical uncertainty; repricing to continue for about a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the one-quarter INR100 crore management overlay increase run through P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the INR100 crore additional ECL provision is charged to P&L; without it profit would be INR100 crore higher. Overlay retained at INR220 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the dividend paid when profit growth was ~13%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capital adequacy (25.5%) is comfortable and the company is underleveraged, so INR2.50 per share was seen as a fair return to shareholders.

qa_highlights.question: Will receivables growth accelerate in FY27 or only FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No asset growth guidance was given; management reiterated that asset growth will follow card acquisition at 0.9-1.0 million per quarter.

risks_watch: Revolver ratio (22%) drifting lower; instalment book offset is not expected to fully compensate; NIM at risk from cost-of-funds rise.
Receivables growth at ~2% YoY; no guidance given on asset growth.
Opex and cost-to-income: Q4 adjusted cost-to-income near 60% after one-offs; FY27 guidance 55-58%.
Geopolitical and macro uncertainty affecting credit cost moderation and the pace of ECL model refresh.
Q4 YoY instalment decline and loss of Apple offer; management called these transient, within 3-6 months.
Recovery pool (~INR190 crore) and write-offs trending lower; not disclosed in size.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and profitability trends, but cautious and non-committal on growth, cost of funds and revolver mix, repeatedly declining to quantify FY27 asset growth and cost of funds.
key_quotes: Overall, the business is profitable, but the margins are comparatively thinner, which basically boost both on the cost and the income side.
So we are building on card acquisition, and we expect that the asset growth will follow the card acquisition growth.
We are underleveraged actually, if you look at that.
we are aiming towards 4% to 4.5% of ROA in the medium term. And that is achievable and we are working towards it.

growth.why: No revenue or receivables growth guidance; FY27 guidance covers only cost-to-income (55-58%), stable NIM and moderating credit cost, with receivables growth (~2% YoY in Q4) tied to card acquisition of roughly 0.9-1.0 million accounts a quarter and no capacity or capex disclosed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Credit cost expected to moderate further (Q4 gross credit cost 7.7%, down 55 bps QoQ) and ROA target 4-4.5% medium term, but NIM guided stable and cost-to-income 55-58% (FY26 55.3%) leaves little room for expansion.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Card acquisition of ~917,000 new accounts in Q4 with next quarter expected in a similar 0.9-1.0 million range, but receivables only ~2% YoY and no asset growth guidance given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex plans, capacity or utilisation data discussed; only AI/ML investment mentioned with no amount or timeline.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Only stable NIM, moderating credit cost and cost-to-income held at 55-58%; no revenue or receivables growth guidance, and receivables grew only ~2% YoY to INR56,926 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revolver rate (22%) drifting lower and NIM at risk from cost-of-funds rise (Q4 cost of funds 6.4%, ~70-75% of borrowings floating), with FY27 cost-to-income guided at 55-58% versus FY26 55.3% and Q4 near 60% adjusted.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launches discussed beyond instalment lending as an offset to revolver decline.

rows.label: Instalment lending as revolver offset
rows.why: Management leaning on instalment lending to offset revolver rate drift from 22-24%, though it is not expected to fully compensate and Q4 instalment saw a YoY decline.

rows.label: Underleveraged balance sheet with 25.5% CAR
rows.why: CAR 25.5% and management calls the company underleveraged, implying headroom for faster growth if acquisition converts into receivables, but no growth guidance was given.

rows.label: Corporate-spend passback costs normalise
rows.why: Management said cost-to-income guided at 55-58% as passback costs normalise after FY26 opex rose 22% YoY, with Q4 cost-to-income at 57.2%.

tone.note: Management was confident on asset quality (GNPA 2.41%, credit cost 7.7%) and profitability, but cautious and non-committal on receivables growth, cost of funds and revolver mix, declining to quantify FY27 asset growth; analysts pressed on revolver downside and growth.
